How correlated errors limit averaging

Synthetic equal-variance, zero-mean errors. Individual RMSE is 1; correlation and variance are held fixed while k changes. This is an illustrative calculation, not a fitted TabM result.

Number of submodels k 
Pairwise error correlation ρ (0 = uncorrelated, 1 = perfectly correlated) 
Individual relative RMSE = 1.00  ·  collective relative RMSE = √(0.30 + (1−0.30)/32) = 0.567

In this calculation, averaging reduces RMSE by 43.3%. The floor as k→∞ is √ρ = 0.55, set by correlation, not by k. Real submodels can also have shared bias, unequal variances and correlations that change with k. Measure their errors before applying this explanation.

In this calculation, averaging reduces RMSE by 0.0%. With one member, there is nothing to average. Its training parameterization can still differ from a plain MLP.
